description: Machine-readable token tables for the BWW (Bagpipe Music Writer) file format. See SPEC.md.
headerLines: Bagpipe Reader:1.0 (or Bagpipe Music Writer Gold:1.0, Bagpipe Musicworks Gold:1.0)

textTags.meaning: Footer, e.g. a band name or copyright (drawn when the layout has a footer)
Inline text above a staff, e.g. part or variation names
Free text placed at page coordinates

patterns.meaning: Melody note: pitch, optional beam mark (r starts or continues a beam, l ends it), then the written value (1 whole … 32 thirty-second).
Time signature, count_unit (2_4, 6_8 …). Usually right after the key signature on the first staff.
Dot (') or double dot ('') on the note before it. The pitch is where the dot is drawn, which is often not the note's pitch; it is ignored.
Accidental on the next note. sharpf and sharpc at the start of a staff are the key signature instead. Letters ignore accidentals.
Fermata (pause) over the note before it.
Start of a first or second time ending. '1 first time, '2 second time, '22…'28 second of n (labelled 2 of 3), '224 second and fourth (2 of 2 & 4). Closed by _'.
Tuplet bracket: ^3s … ^3e is a triplet (3 in the time of 2), ^2s … ^2e a duplet (2 in the time of 3), ^53s … ^53e five in the time of three.
Old style triplet: closes a triplet of the three notes before it (the pitch is where the 3 is drawn).
Old style tie, written after the first of the two tied notes (the pitch is where the tie is drawn).

tokens.meaning: Starts a staff (one printed line of music). Each music line of the file begins with it.
Key signature sharp on F; written after & on every staff. Pipe tunes always have sharpf sharpc.
tokens.example: & sharpf sharpc 4_4 D_4 E_4 F_4 HG_4 !t

tokens.meaning: Key signature sharp on C.
tokens.example: & sharpf sharpc 4_4 D_4 E_4 F_4 HG_4 !t

tokens.meaning: Common time, read as 4/4.
Cut time, read as 2/2.
A second time signature later in the tune (a meter change).
Barline.
Barline that ends a staff line.
Double barline.
Double barline that ends a staff line.
Repeat start (barline with dots on the right).
Repeat start without the dots in the token (same meaning as I!'').
Repeat end.
Repeat end that ends a staff line.
End of a part or the tune (thin-thick barline).
End barline that ends a staff line.
First time ending starts.
Second time ending starts.
Closes the open ending, or else the open singling, doubling, bis or introduction bracket, at the end of its bar.
Singling bracket: drawn like an ending over the bars up to _'. Playback ignores it.
Doubling bracket, as 'si.
Introduction bracket, as 'si.
Bis (play twice) bracket, closed by bis_' (sometimes _').
Ends a bis bracket. Some files also write it inside endings, where it changes nothing.
tokens.example: & 4_4 'bis D_4 E_4 F_4 HG_4 bis_' ! D_4 E_4 F_4 HG_4 !t

tokens.meaning: Tie start, before the first tied note.
Tie end, after the second tied note.
Triplet starts.
Triplet ends.
Duplet starts (2 in the time of 3).
Whole rest (an alias of REST_1 seen in real files).
Half rest (an alias of REST_2 seen in real files).
Natural on the next C.
Natural on the next F.
An alias of naturalc seen in real files.
Flat on the next C.
Fermata on the D before it.
Fine (end here after the da capo).
tokens.example: & 4_4 D_4 E_4 F_4 HG_4 !t & D_4 E_4 F_4 HG_4 fine !I

tokens.meaning: D.C. al Fine.
tokens.example: & 4_4 D_4 E_4 F_4 HG_4 !t & D_4 E_4 F_4 HG_4 dacapoalfine !I

tokens.meaning: D.S. (back to the segno).
tokens.example: & 4_4 D_4 E_4 F_4 HG_4 !t & D_4 E_4 F_4 HG_4 dalsegno !I

tokens.meaning: D.C. al Coda.
tokens.example: & 4_4 D_4 E_4 F_4 HG_4 !t & D_4 E_4 F_4 HG_4 dacapoalcoda !I

tokens.meaning: Segno sign.
Coda sign.
Coda sign where the coda section starts (drawn as coda).
Taorluath abbreviation: a T under the note before. ptb, phtla, ptlg, ptbrea and the other pt…/pht… names draw the same.
Crunluath abbreviation: a c under the note before. pcb, phcla, pclg and the other pc…/phc… names draw the same.
Lemluath abbreviation: an L under the note before. plb, phlla and the other pl…/phl… names draw the same.
Extra horizontal space (Bagpipe Music Writer layout only).
A barline typed with no space before the next note's gracenote; read as ! then gg.
